description:
About Us
HireHawk connects skilled professionals around the world with meaningful remote opportunities supporting U.S. and Canadian companies. We focus on long-term placements where experienced professionals can take real ownership, become trusted members of the team, and make a measurable impact from anywhere.
About the Role
As a Medical Administrative & Surgical Patient Coordinator, you will own the administrative coordination that happens after a patient begins moving through the surgical process. You will make sure required clearances, testing, records, appointments, documentation, and pre-operative steps are completed so patients stay on track for surgery.
This is an operations-focused healthcare role, not a sales position and not a remote clinical position. You will work directly with patients, medical offices, imaging centers, laboratories, hospitals, and other healthcare providers while knowing when a question or concern needs to be escalated to clinical staff. You will receive training on the practice's specific workflows and gradually take ownership of a critical part of the patient journey.
Responsibilities

• Own and track the pre-operative process for multiple surgical patients from booking through readiness for surgery.

• Keep each patient's pre-operative checklist current, identifying missing clearances, tests, records, documentation, and other requirements before they become delays.

• Coordinate required appointments and testing, including imaging, medical clearances, laboratory work, and other pre-operative requirements.

• Contact hospitals, imaging centers, laboratories, physicians' offices, and other healthcare facilities to obtain outstanding information and keep cases moving.

• Follow up persistently with outside providers when testing, records, or clearances are delayed, advocating for patients while maintaining professional communication.

• Conduct or support standardized pre-operative patient calls and clearly walk patients through established non-clinical instructions and next steps.

• Maintain accurate documentation of patient conversations, completed requirements, pending items, and case status within the appropriate systems.

• Communicate surgical readiness, outstanding requirements, and potential delays clearly to the broader practice team.

• Recognize clinical questions, unusual circumstances, or concerns that fall outside your administrative scope and escalate them promptly rather than providing independent medical advice.

• Provide additional medical administrative and patient-coordination support when needed to improve the efficiency of the surgical process.

Requirements

Must-Have:

• 3+ years of experience in medical administration, surgical coordination, patient coordination, pre-operative coordination, or closely related healthcare operations.

• Hands-on experience working in a U.S. medical practice or healthcare environment.

• Direct experience coordinating surgical or pre-operative patients, including appointments, tests, medical records, clearances, or required documentation.

• Experience using EMR, CRM, patient-management, or comparable medical-office systems.

• Confidence communicating directly with patients and contacting hospitals, imaging centers, laboratories, physicians' offices, and other healthcare providers.

• Excellent spoken and written English, with strong documentation, organization, case-tracking, and follow-through skills.

• Sound judgment regarding administrative versus clinical responsibilities, including knowing when an issue must be escalated to clinical staff.

Nice to Have:

• Experience in plastic surgery, cosmetic surgery, aesthetics, or another high-touch private-pay medical environment.

• Medical Assistant training, nursing-related education, healthcare education, or equivalent clinical-office experience.

• Experience conducting standardized pre-operative patient calls.

title: Scientist II / Senior Scientist, Electron Diffraction Characterization

Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is seeking a Scientist II / Senior Scientist, Electron Diffraction Characterization to join the Materials Science team within the Autonomous Science Platform. The Autonomous Science Platform combines experimental science, automation, AI, and software to accelerate materials discovery. This role turns electron diffraction and microstructure measurements into trusted, machine-readable data that supports crystal structure determination, materials characterization, automated workflows, and model development.

You will lead method development, validation, and operation for electron diffraction characterization workflows, with emphasis on micro-ED and/or EBSD. You will prepare samples, run measurements, interpret diffraction and microstructure data, troubleshoot data-quality issues, and establish workflows that make characterization outputs accurate, reproducible, and fit for purpose.

You will also translate electron diffraction expertise into scalable analyzer pipelines. Partnering with ML, software, automation, and experimental teams, you will define metadata, quality-control checks, provenance, and analysis workflows that make diffraction data reliable, traceable, and useful at scale.

The ideal candidate combines deep hands-on expertise in electron diffraction characterization with strong scientific judgment and a commitment to high-quality data. They can operate at the instrument, interpret complex structural and microstructural outputs, and help build the analytical infrastructure needed to scale characterization across Lila’s platform.

What You'll Be Building

• Lead micro-ED and other electron microscopy characterization workflows for materials discovery programs.

• Develop methods for crystal structure determination and microstructure analysis.

• Prepare samples, run measurements, interpret data, and troubleshoot quality issues.

• Define calibration, validation, QC, and reproducibility standards for electron diffraction workflows.

• Build structured, traceable diffraction outputs for downstream analysis and modeling.

• Partner with ML, software, automation, and experimental teams on analyzer pipelines.

• Translate project needs into fit-for-purpose characterization methods and analysis plans.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• PhD in Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics, Applied Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or M.S. with equivalent hands-on characterization experience.

• Hands-on expertise in SEM and TEM including advanced diffraction analysis such as micro-ED.

• Strong understanding of diffraction principles, crystallography, crystal structure determination, and microstructure analysis.

• Experience preparing samples, validating methods, interpreting diffraction data, and troubleshooting workflow issues.

• Ability to translate characterization workflows into reliable, structured, machine-readable data.

• Experience collaborating across scientific, ML, software, automation, or data teams.

• Clear communication skills for documenting methods, explaining results, and driving cross-functional decisions.

Bonus Points For

• Experience with other EM techniques including EBSD, 4D-STEM is a plus.

• Familiarity with automated or high-throughput characterization workflows.

• Proficiency with Python or similar tools for scientific data analysis.

• Experience integrating instrument data with ML-ready datasets or analyzer workflows.

title: Senior Principal Inbound Product Manager, CRM Voice AI
description:
How We Work:
We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency. A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one. Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.
Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.
What This Role Owns:

• You run one pod directly - one of our most complex customer engagements - and float across two others, providing product direction and unblocking teams. But the pod work is only half the job.

• Your primary technical focus is the conversational experience itself: dialog quality, turn-taking, interruption handling, barge-in behavior, and endpointing. You collaborate directly with the platform voice team on voice pipeline innovation, the low-latency infrastructure that makes a voice agent feel like a conversation rather than a bot reading a script. When the platform team is making stack decisions about real-time streaming, LLM orchestration, or voice-to-voice model integration, you're in the room with production customer data and real-world edge cases that no one else has.

• You also own an industry vertical. title: Robotics Operations Engineer I, First Shift
description:
Your Impact at LILA

The Robotics Operations Engineer supports deployment and day-to-day operation of Lila’s production robot fleet. This role is the front-line technical presence for robots operating in production environments, ensuring safe, reliable operation and rapid response when issues arise.

You’ll monitor live robot operations, perform hands-on troubleshooting, document incidents clearly, and partner with robotics software and hardware teams to improve uptime. The role is based in a lab production environment and will help support expanded fleet operating hours as the team scales. This role begins on a standard 9am-5pm schedule and transitions to first shift coverage, 6am-2pm, as fleet operating hours expand.

What You'll Be Building

• Monitor robot behavior during live production operations.

• Intervene quickly and safely to pause, stop, or reset robots when needed.

• Document logs, sensor output, video, and reproduction steps for incident escalation.

• Perform minor robot maintenance, including cabling, sensor swaps, fasteners, and basic component replacement.

• Execute robot swap procedures, validate spare units, and return robots to production readiness.

• Maintain accurate records of robot health, incidents, maintenance actions, and fleet status.

• Translate field observations into clear priorities for robotics software and hardware fixes.

• Identify recurring failure patterns and recommend improvements that reduce downtime.

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Hands-on experience working with robotic systems through work experience, technical programs, internships, academic robotics teams, or equivalent practical exposure.

• Solid grasp of core robotics concepts, including kinematics, sensors, actuators, and control systems.

• Working experience with ROS2, including nodes, topics, launch files, and debugging or introspection tools.

• Comfortable with basic mechanical and electrical troubleshooting, including cabling, connectors, sensors, and fasteners.

• Strong observational skills and sound judgment for quick, safe decisions during live operation.

• Clear written communication skills for documenting issues and reporting to engineering teams.

• Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

• Flexibility to begin on a standard 9am-5pm schedule and transition to first shift coverage, 6am-2pm, as fleet operating hours expand.

Bonus Points For

• Experience supporting robots or automated systems through a production rollout or pilot phase.

• Familiarity with Nav2, Behavior Trees, or related robotics tooling.

• Scripting experience with Python or similar tools for log review, data collection, or simple automation.

• Experience with fleet management, monitoring dashboards, telemetry tools, or issue-tracking systems.

• Background in mechanical, electrical, robotics, or mechatronics engineering through a degree, technical program, or equivalent hands-on experience.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

title: (Freelance) Senior Backend Engineer (m/f/d) - Agent SDK
description:
🎤 Why voize? Because we're more than just a job!

At voize, we believe the greatest gift to frontline workers is time - time to care, connect, and be present. Today, that time is lost to busywork and complex systems that pull them away from what matters most: people.

Our vision is to change that by building AI companions that seamlessly take over digital workflows. We don't replace humans with technology - we amplify their impact.

Our mission is backed with a $50M Series A funding led by Balderton Capital, with support from HV Capital, Y Combinator and other leading VCs. Today, 2,000+ facilities trust voize, and over 200,000 users rely on our AI companion to ease their daily workload.

As a dynamic team, we combine first-in-class technology with meaningful social impact. And now, we're looking for you to join us on this mission!

💡 Your Mission: Build the layer every agent moves onto

As Senior Backend Engineer on the team behind our Agent SDK, you build and maintain the Kotlin foundation that our AI agents move onto. Agents have grown into a product surface across verticals and markets, and the layer underneath them needs a permanent owner. Your work makes the cost of the second and third agents visibly less than the first, so feature teams can ship at their own pace.

🚀 Your Daily Business - No two days are alike

- Build and maintain the SDK as an internal product. You shape the runtime and the client-facing contracts that consuming teams build on. The SDK has a roadmap of its own, and you help set it.

- You build the identity layer that agents run on, so customer-facing agents can write with a real user identity. Your responsibilities may include designing and shipping the auth plumbing, depending on what we have already built by your start date.

- Make every agent observable from the day it launches. You wire telemetry and error reporting into the SDK by default, and you integrate inference and anonymization so the SDK enforces them for every consumer.

- Build the test kit that the SDK still needs. You create it along with the architecture tests that protect the runtime internals, and you build the path that runs every SDK agent against our ML team's evaluation harness before a model change ships.

- Absorb ecosystem change on behalf of consuming teams. You own Koog version bumps and format compatibility, and you set the shared limits on tool output and token usage, so an upgrade lands once in the SDK and reaches everyone from there.

🤝 Your Skillset - What you bring to the table

- Several years of production backend experience on the JVM - Kotlin, Java, Scala or similar. Our stack is Kotlin, and you are ready to work in it.

- You have designed APIs that other engineers build against. An SDK or an internal platform where the contract is the product.

- You have built and maintained integrations, and kept them stable when the system on the other side changed.

- Testing and observability are part of how you build.

- You are drawn to AI agent systems, and to the orchestration and evaluation work underneath them.

🌱 Growing together - what you can expect at voize

- We are a fast-growing startup, that means you will take on real problems, grow quickly, and make a real impact, giving frontline workers more time for people

As Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Compute, you will own payment readiness and material exceptions across large-value, business-critical obligations. Complex agreements evolve through amendments to pricing, capacity, service credits, billing mechanics, legal entities, and payment schedules. You will translate approved obligations into accurate, timely payments while navigating supplier disputes, late approvals, close deadlines, and cross-system dependencies.

title: In-Home Health - Physician (Part Time)- Hartford, CT
description:
Job Title: In-Home Health - Physician (Part Time)- Hartford, CT
Job Location: Work at Home, Connecticut, United States
Job Location Type: Remote
Job Contract Type: Part time
Job Seniority Level:
We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

Part-time employees qualify for:

• Select benefits (see benefits guide for details)

• Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

• Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

• Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

• Multi-state licenses (preferred)

• Able to cover the following primary locations: Hartford and surroun

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Overview
LMI is seeking a Platform Engineer to design, deploy, operate, and sustain secure cloud-native platform capabilities for a Department of War mission partner. This remote role will focus on Amazon Web Services (AWS)-hosted Kubernetes environments that connect to and operate within the Department of Defense Information Network (DODIN). The Platform Engineer will support platform architecture, infrastructure automation, container orchestration, application onboarding, cybersecurity compliance, observability, troubleshooting, and continuous service improvement. The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who can translate mission and application requirements into reliable, repeatable, secure, and supportable platform services.
LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.
Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors, helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.
This is a remote position within the continental United States and requires an active Secret security clearance. The employee must be available during core working hours aligned to the mission partner and may be required to travel periodically to government or LMI locations for integration, testing, maintenance, or mission support.
Responsibilities

• Design, deploy, configure, operate, and sustain AWS-based platform services supporting mission-critical Department of War applications and workloads.

• Administer Kubernetes clusters and supporting services, including cluster configuration, node groups, namespaces, role-based access control, ingress, service discovery, storage, secrets management, network policies, autoscaling, upgrades, and lifecycle maintenance.

• Build and maintain repeatable infrastructure and platform configurations using infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, or equivalent customer-approved technologies.

• Develop, maintain, and improve continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, GitOps workflows, container registries, artifact repositories, automated testing, and deployment controls.

• Onboard, configure, deploy, and sustain containerized applications across development, test, staging, and production environments.

• Integrate platform services with DODIN network services, identity and access management, public key infrastructure, logging, monitoring, vulnerability management, endpoint security, and other government enterprise services.

• Implement and maintain secure platform configurations aligned with approved security baselines, Defense Information Systems Agency Security Technical Implementation Guides, Risk Management Framework requirements, and Authority to Operate conditions.

• Monitor platform availability, performance, capacity, security posture, and application health using AWS-native and customer-approved observability tools.

• Troubleshoot complex issues involving Linux, containers, Kubernetes, AWS services, networking, Domain Name System, certificates, encryption, load balancing, storage, compute, identity, and application dependencies.

• Perform platform patching, vulnerability remediation, configuration management, backup, recovery, and controlled upgrade activities while minimizing mission disruption.

• Collaborate with cybersecurity, network, software, data, systems engineering, and mission teams to resolve dependencies and deliver integrated capabilities.

title: Account Specialist
description:
About Us:

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.

About the Role:

We’re looking for a true startup Operations person. Good onboarding is what makes our merchants set up for success. From the first meeting, the go-live to working and growing together - this person will own the onboarding process and make it all happen. This role is for someone who likes working with the product, becoming an expert in it and teaching others.

Your day-to-day will be a mix of hands-on ops, project management, customer communication and problem solving. We are reshaping the future of hospitality tech, and this role is at the forefront of it.

What You’ll Do:

Our Operations happen on a restaurant floor, in a lively neighbourhood, at a busy bar - we operate in the city:

- Run restaurant onboarding: train, connect and implement together with the restaurant team

- Problem-solve for our merchants on the ground while running live operations

- Support restaurants for the first month after the go live

- Find opportunities for improvement in our process, materials and systems

- Identify product and process gaps and bring it to internal central teams such as product, engineering and central operations

What You’ll Need:

- You are a creative problem solver who enjoys interacting with hospitality businesses

- You are empathetic towards our merchants and curious about their business

- You can juggle multiple things at once and bring structure

- Curious about the product, want to be an expert in Tebi system and can apply your knowledge

- Good communication - you are great at proactive contact and managing expectations

- Being comfortable with high-pace environments: both the hospitality flow and the startup day-to-day

- Flexibility in working hours to fit our merchants’ needs

- At least 1-2 years of experience in hospitality, early startup operations, fast-paced account management or customer operations

- You are comfortable working in both Danish and English

If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careershttps://www.tebi.com/de/careers.

Benefits:

- Start-up Equity

- Competitive Salary

- Flexible Time-off

- Team events

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

title: Senior SoC Architect (f/m/d)
description:
About us

We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects

About our technology

The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude

In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution

The Role

We are seeking a skilled Senior SoC Architect at Black Semiconductor to drive the architecture of our entire Electronics-Photonics IC (EPIC) SoC, translating the Marketing Requirement Document (MRD) into a complete, internally consistent, and implementable Product Requirement Document (PRD) covering digital, analog, I/O, and memory subsystems.

You will own the digital and high-speed I/O subsystem architecture directly, with particular depth in high-speed SerDes and the protocol digital logic for UCIe, PCIe, and Ethernet. Working closely with the Analog/RF System Architect, Photonics System Architect, Package Electrical/SI Architect, memory subsystem owner, product management, and engineering teams, you will integrate their subsystem architectures into one coherent overall product architecture.

To join our team, you should be excited to

- Own the overall EPIC SoC technical leadership from initial concept through production and drive cross-functional technical alignment across photonics, analog, digital, technology, and product teams.

- Build and document the overall product architecture, translating the MRD into a complete PRD and ensuring architectural decisions, technical requirements, dependencies, and trade-offs are consistently aligned across teams.

- Own the digital subsystem architecture, including core logic, on-chip interconnect fabric, and subsystem partitioning.

- Own the high-speed I/O subsystem architecture, with particular depth in high-speed SerDes and the protocol digital logic for UCIe, PCIe, and Ethernet, including how protocol layers map onto the physical SerDes implementation.

- Partner with the Analog/RF System Architect, Photonics System Architect, Package Electrical/SI Architect, and memory subsystem owner to integrate their architectures and ensure the full-chip architecture is internally consistent and feasible within the target electrical, physical, and packaging constraints.

- Drive full-chip performance, power, and area (PPA) trade-off analysis, partner with external vendors/3rd-party IP providers on full-chip validation and characterization teams on product characterization, and make the calls needed to keep the PRD internally consistent.

- Present the integrated architecture and PRD to product management and engineering leadership and own it through to sign-off.

Your Qualifications

ESSENTIAL

- 7-10 years of experience in SoC or product architecture roles, with proven SoC/product architecture ownership and demonstrated experience taking a product from MRD-level requirements through a complete, implementable PRD-level architecture covering multiple subsystems and at least one full product architecture cycle.

- Deep, hands-on high-speed I/O subsystem expertise, parti

Esta cultura inclusiva se fomenta a través de diversos grupos de recursos para empleados (ERG) y eventos frecuentes en la oficina para destacar los logros del equipo, compartir liderazgo de pensamiento y celebrar fechas especiales e hitos importantes. Nuestro paquete integral de beneficios refleja este compromiso e incluye seguro médico, de visión y dental, planes grupales de retiro, un generoso programa de tiempo libre pagado, descuentos preferenciales con aliados y días dedicados al bienestar y la salud mental de nuestro equipo.

En WPP Media ofrecemos igualdad de oportunidades y consideramos todas las postulaciones sin discriminación. Creemos que el mejor trabajo surge cuando estamos juntos, potenciando la creatividad, la colaboración y la conexión en un entorno abierto y colaborativo. Ten en cuenta que, si bien nuestra filosofía es la misma en todo WPP, los beneficios específicos pueden variar según la oficina o el país.

Por favor, consulta nuestro Aviso de Privacidad ( https://www.wppmedia.com/pages/privacy-policy ) para obtener más información sobre cómo procesamos la información que nos proporcionas.

title: Strategy and Operations, OpenAI for Government
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The OpenAI for Government team is a dynamic, mission-driven group leveraging frontier AI to transform how governments achieve their missions. Our team works to empower public servants with secure, compliant AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise in custom configurations) and mission-aligned deployments that meet government technical requirements with strong reliability and safety.

As part of the OpenAI for Government team you will work across governments and public institutions, helping to accelerate adoption through hands-on support, tailored training, and early insights-so civil servants can spend less time on red tape and more on meaningful work. If you're passionate about responsibly deploying frontier AI to uplift public institutions and transform how the government serves the American people, we want you on our team.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced strategy and business operations professional to help OpenAI for Government decide where to grow and how to build the capabilities needed to serve government customers. You will shepherd ambiguous, complex work from problem definition through execution. The majority of the role will focus on business strategy and operations, from market and revenue planning to workforce, financial, and secure facility initiatives. You should be skilled at both developing a compelling recommendation and doing the detailed work to make it happen.

This role has four key buckets of responsibilities:

- First, you will support the growth and maturation of a business operations and revenue strategy function within the OpenAI for Government. You will help OpenAI for Government four vertical leaders develop annual business strategies that define target customers, priority projects, partners, and support needed from other matrixed teams including Technical Success, Engineering, Capture and Proposal, Global Affairs, and Product Policy.

- You will build and maintain the intelligence picture for our key territories: mission priorities, budget lines and program timelines, incumbents and competitive positions, and the people who actually shape awards.

- You will act as a thought partner to the business verticals by participating in weekly team discussions to understand the business, test assumptions, and identify risks. You will run quarterly reviews to track progress, reassess goals, and adjust priorities.

- Second, you will partner with OpenAI’s industrial security team to forecast secure-space needs, plan SCIF buildouts, coordinate personnel access nominations, and track contract-specific security requirements and restrictions.

- Third, you will support OpenAI’s Government Innovation Network, OpenAI for Government’s advisory board, throughout the entire lifecycle of the program, including advisor outreach and selection, independent-contractor agreements (1099s), conflict reviews, payment, and high-touch onboarding.

- In partnership with OpenAI for Government’s leadership team, you will help design and run regular advisor meetings, quarterly strategy sessions, and targeted convenings, with clear agendas, materials, and decisions. You will execute follow-through, and ensure advisor insights are integrated into OpenAI for Government’s strategy.

- Finally, you will own and drive special projects that do not yet have a clear home. You will define the problem, develop options, build consensus, and lead early execution.

YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

- Have experience in strategy consulting, business operations, a growing technology company, or comparable work combining analytical problem-solving with ownership of execution.

- Can build financial models, size markets, assess competitive positions, and translate incomplete data into recommendations with clear assumptions and tradeoffs. Are comfortable interpreting government budgets and using market intelligence sources such as Janes to inform long-term investment decisions.

- Create compelling executive presentatio

title: Director of Instructional Design

About the role

Alchemy is looking for a hands-on Director of Instructional Design to lead how our customers and our design team get the most out of Curie, Alchemy's AI-enabled course design software dedicated to reducing costs, accelerating course and program development, and driving educational outcomes. You will be the instructional design voice of the company: coaching customers as they roll Curie out to their faculty, setting the standards our designers work to, and making sure the ID work we sell is scoped, staffed, and delivered well.

This is a player-coach role. You will lead a distributed team of instructional designers, including contractors, while still rolling up your sleeves on customer training, product testing, and proposal work. You will partner closely with the Director of Project Management and the VP of Product Development.

What you'll do

Customer enablement

• Advise and train customers on implementing Curie with their faculty, including onboarding sessions, workshops, and faculty-facing guidance.

• Speak credibly to instructional design principles and best practices with customers, faculty, and academic leaders.

• Create and maintain training materials, job aids, and implementation guides for Curie.

Team leadership

• Provide day-to-day direction to a distributed team of instructional designers, including employees and contractors, all working remotely.

• Set scope for instructional design development on each project and assign work accordingly.

• Recruit, hire, and onboard qualified instructional designers and contractors as project demand requires.

• Give regular, constructive feedback and review work for quality and consistency.

Standards and quality

• Establish and maintain instructional design standards for work built with Alchemy and Curie.

• Ensure course designs meet accessibility and quality expectations, such as WCAG and Quality Matters.

Product partnership

• Serve as the instructional design subject-matter expert for the Product Development team, weighing in on features and roadmap when asked.

• Test and QA new Curie features and releases from an instructional designer's and faculty user's point of view.

• Bring customer feedback and field insights back to the product team.

Scoping and delivery

• Scope the instructional design portion of RFPs and proposals using the Alchemy product catalog.

• Partner with the Director of Project Management to deliver projects within scope, budget, and timeline.

• Work with the Director of Project Management to design repeatable, scalable approaches for large or multi-course projects.

• Coordinate with outside vendors and partners when projects require it.

• Lead projects as the instructional designer yourself when the situation warrants it.

What you bring

• Master's degree in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Education, or a related field (bachelor's with equivalent experience considered).

• 5+ years of instructional design experience in higher education, including online and hybrid course development.

• 2+ years leading or directing instructional designers, including remote team members or contractors.

• Strong command of instructional design models and learning science, such as ADDIE, backward design, and UDL.

• Experience training or consulting with faculty and academic stakeholders.

• Experience scoping ID work for proposals, statements of work, or project estimates.

• Working knowledge of multiple LMSs, such as Canvas, Blackboard, D2L Brightspace, or Moodle.

• Clear, confident communication and presentation skills with both technical and academic audiences.

• Comfort testing software and giving structured, actionable feedback to product teams.

• Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1/2.2) and accessibility testing.

• Experience using AI tools as well as design and interactive creation tools such as the articulate suite, h5p, etc.

Nice to have

• Experience in workforce development or corporate learn

description:

We are hiring a Senior Compliance Analyst, Snowgov Compliance for our SnowTrust GRC team. You will champion key public sector compliance initiatives, safeguard Snowflake's US public sector certifications, and align IT, Legal, Product, Security, and Engineering around the work that powers Snowflake's growth in government markets.

AS A SENIOR COMPLIANCE ANALYST, SNOWGOV COMPLIANCE AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

- Own and maintain core FedRAMP authorization artifacts, including the System Security Plan (SSP), Contingency Plan (ISCP), and Incident Response Plan (IRP), keeping them accurate and updated annually.

- Manage the lifecycle of Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M), tracking findings, risks, and remediation commitments through closure with clear ownership and realistic deadlines.

- Coordinate annual 3PAO assessments and continuous monitoring, acting as the primary liaison between Snowflake, assessors, and federal agency stakeholders.

- Advise Engineering and Operations teams so cloud configurations (FIPS 140-3 validation, boundary protection, access control, logging and monitoring) meet federal and DoD mandates.

- Perform gap analyses for new or evolving public sector requirements, such as emerging CMMC or GovRAMP mandates and FedRAMP Consolidated Rules, and define technical remediation roadmaps.

- Respond to customer and regulator inquiries about Snowflake's public sector security and compliance obligations, and build self-service resources so customers and field teams can increasingly answer these questions themselves.

OUR IDEAL SENIOR COMPLIANCE ANALYST, SNOWGOV COMPLIANCE WILL HAVE:

- 5+ years of experience in risk management, compliance, GRC, or a related governance function within a regulated or public sector environment preferred.

- Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 controls and the FedRAMP authorization process.

- Experience contributing to SSPs, POA&Ms, contingency plans (ISCP), and incident response plans (IRP).

- Experience writing and maintaining audit-ready governance artifacts, including policies, standards, procedures, and control narratives.

- Experience coordinating with 3PAOs, auditors, or assessors during annual assessments or continuous monitoring cycles.

- Ability to influence stakeholders across Engineering, IT, Legal, and Security to drive control implementation and remediation without direct authority.

- Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent audit and assessment timelines and track findings through closure.

- Experience using AI to automate or streamline manual compliance workflows.

BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING:

- CISSP, CISM, CISA, or other information security certifications

- Experience with DoD Impact Level authorizations and CMMC certification

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.
